title: Traffic Orchestra: Friction Points Inventory & Operator Runbook (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, operator-facing inventory of repeated friction points we hit when running cross-functional canaries and A/Bs across Console, Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Goal: reduce coordination latency by documenting symptoms, pragmatic mitigations, and a small set of reproducible runbook actions that any steward can execute during a run.

Audience:
- Primary: release stewards / release engineers / rollout owners
- Secondary: PMs, SRE oncall, solutions engineering, CS for customer-sensitive rollouts

Scope:
- Focused on traffic orchestration + human handoffs for canaries / A/Bs (not the model-training lifecycle).
- Includes both technical and coordination friction (tooling + people).

Executive summary (one sentence):
Friction usually stems from three overlapping failure modes — signal lag, ownership ambiguity, and capacity mismatch — and can be dramatically reduced by short, deterministic rituals and a tiny set of pre-authored commands + dashboards.

Friction categories (inventory):
1) Ownership & decision latency
   - Symptoms: delayed approvals, multiple people making simultaneous changes, “whose rollback?” confusion during spike.
   - Root causes: ambiguous steward for cohort changes, insufficiently prescriptive escalation matrix.
   - Quick mitigations: pre-assign a single steward + a backup; attach changes to an explicit ticket with step-by-step rollback checklist; 2-minute phone-tree template.
   - Runbook snippet: "Steward role = release-<feature>-owner@redwood: authorized to flip slices in Console for that canary. Backup = oncall-sre."

2) Signal availability & lag (telemetry gaps)
   - Symptoms: metrics sparse for first 5–20 minutes; dashboards show zeros; discrepancy between tracing and metrics.
   - Root causes: aggregation windows, metric sampling, prefix cache warmup delaying observable effects.
   - Pragmatic mitigations: pre-run synthetic traffic (see smoke below) for 10min; reduce metric rollup window where possible; instrument a fast-signal counter (sampled_events_fast_counter) shipped to the steward's dashboard.
   - Checklist: Confirm fast-signal feed is green -> run 100 synthetic requests -> validate heatmap/population.

3) Model variant compatibility and shadowing mismatches
   - Symptoms: variant returns structured JSON in prod but fallback model returns unstructured text; A/B resulting in higher error rates for one cohort.
   - Root causes: implicit schema drift between model bundles, incompatible function-calling stubs, or different tokenization/stop strategies.
   - Mitigations: require contract tests for each model variant; include a tiny schema-transform shim in fallbacks; add a compatibility flag to the Console rollout UI that blocks cross-variant experiments when schema mismatch is detected.

4) Capacity triage and asymmetric throttling
   - Symptoms: one cohort experiences elevated latency because traffic routed to a saturated Dedicated pool.
   - Root causes: mismatched routing policies, burst capacity not enabled for the pool, or unexpected cold-starts in private deployments.
   - Mitigations: pre-allocate a small burst pool for canaries; enable autoscale policy 'canary-burst=on' for known experiments; have a 'force-reroute' CLI ready to move slices to fallback region.
   - Example operator command (CLI):
       rinf route slice --slice-id=canary-42 --to=region-fallback --force --reason="canary-pool-saturation"

5) Rollback coordination and “partial rollback” confusion
   - Symptoms: half the slices reverted, other half still running; front-end and back-end configs out-of-sync.
   - Root causes: multi-step rollout that lacks atomic revert API, manual steps across services.
   - Mitigations: create a single revert script that calls Console API -> Flush feature flags -> invalidate edge cache -> re-scan telemetry. Version the revert script and include a one-click action in the steward's console.

6) Stakeholder fatigue & meeting overhead
   - Symptoms: too many watchers on the call, slow commit to action, repeated status pings.
   - Mitigations: use a status baton pattern: one person reports facts every 5 minutes; other stakeholders only escalate. Keep the initial call strictly 15 minutes.

7) Metrics alignment (what success looks like)
   - Define primary metric(s) before exposing traffic. Examples: end-to-end latency p50/p95, task success rate, incorrect-output rate, cost-per-1000-tokens.
   - If there are multiple models in play, each must publish the same canonical metric names (task_success_rate_v1, task_success_rate_v2).

Runbook: pre-launch smoke (10 minutes)
- Confirm steward and backup assigned on ticket.
- Confirm experiment config in Console: slices, traffic-weight, rollout-window, fallback.
- Run synthetic load: 200 requests at 1 req/s (with identical prompt set for each variant).
- Validate fast-signal counters, end-to-end tracing, and model contract tests.
- Check capacity: peek atDedicatedPoolUtilization and burst quota.
- Sanity-check sample outputs into a 'review bucket' (S3) and a human reviewer if required.

Launch cadence (suggested minimal choreography)
- T+0: enable 1% traffic, steward notes timestamp and announces in Slack thread (use template message).
- T+10m: confirm fast signals; if green -> increase to 5%; else -> hold and trigger diagnostic script.
- T+30m: decision window to go to 20% or revert. Use explicitly defined metric thresholds (example thresholds below).
- T+2h: if all green, proceed to ramp or follow product plan.

Short post-launch (first 60 minutes) checklist
- Check p50/p95 latency drift > threshold? If p95 rises > +150ms -> trigger immediate partial rollback.
- Task success rate drop > 2 percentage points absolute -> pause ramp.
- Error budget burn: track within Console; 3x baseline error-rate spike -> notify SRE and CS.

Suggested thresholds (example)
- p50 drift: +100ms allowed; p95 drift +150ms -> investigate
- task_success_rate drop: 1% -> investigate, 2% -> pause, 3% -> revert
- infra errors increase (5xx): > 0.5% of requests -> pause

Fast tools (copyable to a steward's playbook)
- Force re-route: rinf route slice --slice-id=%SLICE% --to=%REGION% --force --reason=""
- Quick revert (one-liner): rinf rollout revert --experiment=%EXP% --to=previous --confirm
- Metric snapshot (one-liner): rinf metrics snapshot --exp=%EXP% --window=10m --dest=s3://canary-snapshots/%EXP%/$(date +%s)

Rehearsal & training suggestions
- Monthly microdrills: simulate a canary pause and require the steward to perform forced reroutes and revert. Keep the drill <30 minutes.
- Run a tabletop once per quarter with cross-functional participants: PM, SRE, steward, CS, SLA owner. Capture decisions in the ticket.

Edge-case notes (observed in past runs)
- Private deploys sometimes have hour-long key rotation windows; schedule experiments outside rotation windows.
- A/Bs that touch embeddings (search re-ranking) can surface slow drift only after 24–48h; consider a longer hold for such experiments.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups (next actions)
- Add a 'fast-signal' metric as a standard in Console; current engineers: @Priya to spin up a spec (due 2025-03-12).
- Small UI affordance: a one-click ‘atomic revert’ that funnels through the steward-run API. Product/Console owner: @Liam to scope.
- Define 'canary-burst' autocap policy defaults for Dedicated vs Private. Infra team: @Omar to propose defaults.

Appendix: steward announcement template (Slack)
- Subject: [CANARY] <feature> exp=<exp-id> steward=<name> step=<percent>
- Body: Running 1% to start. Primary metric: task_success_rate. Checkpoint windows: T+10m (fast-signal), T+30m (stability). Revert command: rinf rollout revert --experiment=<exp-id>

Appendix: quick links and bookmarks
- Rollout ticket template: CONFLUENCE-12345
- Experiment runbook (detailed): https://confluence.redwood/rollouts/exp-runbooks/0001
- Slack channel: #rollout-ops

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc short — people will actually read it. Turn long bits into linked short pages.
- Prioritize the fast-signal work; biggest ROI is reducing the initial 10–20m uncertainty.

End of draft.
plain_text_summary: Working inventory of repeated friction points for canary/A-B rollouts; pragmatic runbook snippets, checklists, thresholds, and next-action items assigned to owners. Focus is on operator efficiency and reducing decision latency.
